model.name: Equal-weight combination (ARX + Tier 1 DFM)
model.description: The average of two models that read different panels: a regression on GDP's own last value and a few activity indicators, and a dynamic factor model on the wider Tier 1 panel. Equal weights hedge the choice between them; the live record decides any change.

members.name: ARX on the activity pool
members.description: GDP growth regressed on its own last value and the quarterly growth of Index of Industrial Production - General Index, Index of Core Industries (ICI), Foreign Exchange Reserves - Total, with an overfit guard that leaves out a near-copy of a better indicator.
indicators: Index of Industrial Production - General Index

members.name: Dynamic factor model with GDP lag, Tier 1 panel
members.description: 2 common factors extracted by EM from the 17 Tier 1 monthly indicators, averaged to quarters; GDP growth regressed on them and on its own last value.

caveats: The headline averages two models: a regression on GDP's own last value and 3 activity indicators, and a factor model on the 17 Tier 1 indicators. Neither has yet been shown to beat a naive benchmark in ordinary quarters; the live record from the 2026-27 Q2 release is the test.
The range shown is where past first prints fell around the headline in ordinary conditions, with the COVID years left out. The stress range allows for a miss of the size seen in 2020.
The track record is a backtest: pseudo-real-time, using only figures released before each GDP print but today's revised values, made a week before the print. Live runs are listed separately.
The indicators speak for industry, credit, the external sector and prices. Agriculture, services, household spending beyond fuel and investment demand are not yet covered (see coverage).
Contributions are a static projection; what they leave out, mainly GDP's persistence and the factors' dynamics, is shown as carried forward.
The training sample includes the 2020-2021 COVID quarters, with no adjustment.

evaluation.basis: backtest: pseudo-real-time, first prints, quarters from 2012-13 Q3

selection.definition: Quarters starting through Oct 2019, before COVID.

confirmation.definition: Quarters starting from Jul 2022, after the COVID base effects. 2022-23 Q2 to Q4 have no year-on-year growth, so the first quarter scored is Apr-Jun 2023.

ordinary.definition: Selection and confirmation together: outside the COVID window (quarters starting Jan 2020 to Oct 2021) and the base-effect quarters through Apr 2022. This is the sample the claim that neither model has yet beaten a naive benchmark refers to.

exCovid.definition: Everything outside the COVID window. It adds the two 2022 base-effect quarters to ordinary, on which the AR(1) benchmark missed badly, so every model looks better against it than on ordinary.

gaps.missing: Kharif and rabi sowing and output estimates, monsoon rainfall, tractor and fertiliser sales
gaps.why: Agriculture is roughly a sixth of GVA and has no indicator in either headline model
gaps.candidateSource: Ministry of Agriculture, IMD, FADA and SIAM monthly releases

gaps.missing: Services PMI, air passenger traffic, railway freight and passenger earnings, FASTag toll collections
gaps.why: Services are over half of GVA; the panel holds one bank-credit series and GST
gaps.candidateSource: S&P Global PMI, DGCA, Indian Railways, NHAI

gaps.missing: Passenger-vehicle and two-wheeler sales, UPI transaction value and volume, FMCG volumes
gaps.why: Private consumption is the largest expenditure component; fuel consumption is the only direct measure held
gaps.candidateSource: SIAM and FADA, NPCI (a timely, real-time series), company and industry releases

gaps.why: Investment demand; the IIP use-based capital-goods index is in files already held but not wired as a series
gaps.candidateSource: MoSPI IIP use-based tables (held), Tradestat commodity detail (held, when the site restores it)

gaps.missing: The level of merchandise exports, services exports
gaps.why: Only the export/import ratio is held; exports are in the Tradestat reports already downloaded

gaps.missing: Manufacturing PMI and RBI business and consumer surveys
gaps.why: Survey indicators lead activity and are published within days of the month end

gaps.missing: EPFO payroll additions, MGNREGA work demand
gaps.why: The only labour series are urban and quarterly from 2018

coverage.note: Quarterly shortlisted series (house prices, GFCF, the current account, PLFS) appear here but not in `drivers` or `signals`, which are monthly or finer.
